# QuickRoute

![WoW 12.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/WoW-12.1%20Retail-148EFF)
![Lua](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lua-5.1-2C2D72?logo=lua&logoColor=white)
![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-Lua%205.1%20%2B%20Python-brightgreen)
[![CI](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/CybotTM/wow-quickroute)

A World of Warcraft addon that estimates fast travel routes to map points, quest destinations and dungeon entrances using known teleports, portals and transport connections.

Routes depend on recorded connections, character access and estimated travel times. QuickRoute includes an attributed retail destination catalogue and phase/unlock checks. Terrain, dynamic NPCs and unreported game state can still limit a route. See the [review and coverage report](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/blob/main/docs/REVIEW-2026-09-05.md) for verified behavior and coverage limits.

## What it does for you

- Get to a map pin, a quest objective, a dungeon entrance or a vendor, in steps this character can take.
- Paste a section of a community guide and run it as a trip.
- Find a destination by name when you do not know where it is.
- Refuse a step you cannot use and keep the destination.
- Be told which kind of problem stopped a route, rather than one message for every case.

The distribution listing text lives in [docs/CURSEFORGE-LISTING.md](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/blob/main/docs/CURSEFORGE-LISTING.md).

## Features

- **Smart Pathfinding:** Uses Dijkstra's algorithm to find the lowest estimated travel time in the known graph
- **Route Step Collapsing:** Merges consecutive walk/fly steps into readable directions
- **Teleport Detection:** Scans your inventory, toys, and spells for available teleports
- **Cooldown Tracking:** Considers teleport cooldowns when calculating routes
- **Portal Knowledge:** Includes major portal hubs and recorded transport connections
- **Faction-Aware:** Respects Alliance/Horde restrictions for portals and items
- **Class-Aware:** Includes class-specific teleports (Mage, Druid, Monk, DK, Shaman, DH)
- **Dungeon Teleports:** Mythic+ and attunement teleports route to the dungeon entrance
- **Flight Paths:** Flight masters you have discovered are part of the route graph
- **TomTom Integration:** Automatically detects TomTom waypoints
- **Auto-Destination:** Automatically routes to super-tracked quests/waypoints
- **World Map Teleport Button:** One-click teleport button on the world map
- **Quest Tracker Buttons:** Teleport buttons next to tracked quests
- **Destination Grouping:** Group teleports by destination in the teleport panel
- **POI Click Routing:** Ctrl+Right-click on the world map to route to any location
- **Configurable Settings:** Max cooldown filter, loading screen time, window scale
- **Multi-Destination Trips:** Paste up to 20 waypoints or import active TomTom points; optimize the entire estimated visit order or follow input order; resume saved trips after login
- **Currency Vendors:** Search the included retail vendor catalogue, the Trading Posts (for Trader's Tender) and your character’s merchant observations for a selected currency. Clicking a currency in the character window's Currency tab adds **QuickRoute to vendor** to its options popup when a vendor that accepts it is known (when none is known, **QuickRoute to seller** routes to a merchant you have seen selling the currency, or to an NPC QuickRoute lists for it, such as Orin Straylight for the Nebulous Voidcore); for a Shard of Dundun it reads **QuickRoute to Abundance** and routes to the place of abundance that is active now
- **Quest Discovery:** Search thousands of attributed quest-giver and NPC locations; use live client coordinates for objectives and turn-ins
- **Zone Phases:** Route through seven Zidormi regions with explicit phase changes and visible controls for unknown states
- **Travel Choices:** Discovered Mole Machine stops, selectable engineering destinations, faction garrisons, and observed camp/house locations
- **Access Checks:** Known quest, level, class, faction, reputation and other requirements gate sourced travel connections
- **Automatic Hearth Destination:** Recognize known inns from the client's localized bind name, even before the first use. Morgenluft defaults to its current Midnight version. Observed bindings always take precedence over catalogue approximations and defaults.
- **Acquisition Help:** Click a missing teleport item for its ATT details, or open QuickRoute's source help with requirements and a route when a source position is known
- **Refuse a Step:** A step you cannot use gets a "Cannot use" button. QuickRoute keeps the destination, drops that connection for this route and looks for another way; right-clicking Refresh takes your refusals back
- **Says Why It Failed:** A route that cannot be produced names its reason — position not available yet, something this character does not have, a refused step, or no known connection — because those need different responses from you
- **Bounded Search:** A route for the route panel, a map click, the waypoint command, a dungeon group offer, or another addon through `QuickRouteAPI` is searched in budgeted slices across frames instead of holding the client. Requests from different sources queue rather than cancel each other; a new request from the same source — a second map click, a second request from an addon under the same `owner` — replaces the earlier one. Requests from other addons, and requests without an `owner`, are not replaced. A trip comparison and the quest-tracker buttons start one calculation per frame, which bounds how many run at once rather than what one of them costs. Finding the nearest auction house, bank, void storage or crafting table, or the nearest giver of a quest, still calculates a route for every candidate within the same frame; the currency-vendor search tries one candidate per frame
- **Dungeon Group Offer:** Accepting a group invitation offers the way to that dungeon's entrance, and suspends the trip you were on rather than replacing it
- **For Other Addons:** `QuickRouteAPI` is a versioned contract another addon can ask for a route through, without taking over your arrow (see below)

## Installation

Every release goes to all three at once, from the same build.

| Source | |
|---|---|
| CurseForge | [QuickRoute](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/quickroute) — or search "QuickRoute" in the CurseForge app or WoWUp |
| Wago | [QuickRoute](https://addons.wago.io/addons/quickroute) — or in the WagoApp |
| GitHub | [Latest release](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/releases/latest) |

An addon manager keeps QuickRoute current on its own, which matters here: the addon declares the game version it was built for, and WoW skips an addon whose declared version is behind the live patch unless "Load out of date AddOns" is ticked.

### Manual installation
1. Download `QuickRoute-<version>.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/releases/latest)
2. Extract into `World of Warcraft\_retail_\Interface\AddOns\` so the folder is named `QuickRoute`
3. Restart WoW or `/reload`

## Usage

### Slash Commands
- `/qr` or `/quickroute` - Toggle the route window
- `/qr show` - Show the route window
- `/qr hide` - Hide the route window
- `/qr settings` - Open settings panel
- `/qr minimap` - Toggle minimap button
- `/qr debug` - Toggle debug mode
- `/qr priority mappin|quest|tomtom` - Set the waypoint source priority
- `/qr autowaypoint` - Toggle the automatic waypoint for the first step
- `/qr ah` / `/qr bank` / `/qr void` / `/qr craft` - Route to the nearest auction house, bank, void storage or crafting table
- `/qr currency <ID or exact localized name>` - Route to the fastest known vendor accepting that currency
- `/qr quest <questID> [target|giver]` - Route to the live quest target/turn-in or a known quest giver
- `/qr phases` - Inspect detected phases and set session assumptions when the client cannot report a phase
- `/qr multi` or `/qrmulti` - Open the trip planner; paste `/way #mapID x y` lines with coordinates from 0 to 100. A line such as `50,57 56 Treasure`, where the comma can be a decimal mark or the separator between the two values, shows both readings; pick one before the trip starts
- `/qrmulti tomtom` / `/qrmulti next` / `/qrmulti clear` - Import active TomTom destinations, mark a stop reached, or clear the trip
- `/qrhelp` - Show all commands
- `/qrwp` - Calculate path to current waypoint
- `/qrverifymap [mapID]` - Report what the client and the addon each say about a map
- `/qrpath <mapID> <x> <y>` - Calculate path to coordinates
- `/qrteleports` - Toggle teleport panel
- `/qrdungeons` - Toggle the dungeon and raid picker
- `/qrinv` - Show available teleports
- `/qrcd` - Show teleport cooldowns
- `/qrdebug` - Show waypoint detection info (`/qrdebug copy` yields markdown for bug reports)
- `/qrscreenshot` - Take UI screenshots (`all`, `route`, `teleport`, `search`, `mini`)
- `/qrextract` - Extract data for development (`zones`, `quests`, `portals`, `continent`)

Development commands, not part of the supported surface: `/qrscan`, `/qrgraph`,
`/qrzone`, `/qrdebugpath`, `/qrtest graph`.

### How to Use
1. Set a waypoint on your map (right-click) or use TomTom
2. Type `/qr` to open the route window
3. Follow the step-by-step instructions in the route window

The route list reads as a travel plan: a timeline with one node per step, a header for each continent the route crosses, the current step marked **Now**, and a column on the right with the travel time and labelled buttons for the current step (**Use**, **Set waypoint**, **Step not possible**). The **?** button opens a help overlay that numbers and explains each control; it also opens by itself the first time the route window is shown. **Compact** in the toolbar switches to a small tracker beside the minimap that lists the current step with its action and the steps ahead by continent; its **Window** button switches back, and route requests open whichever view you used last. The window and the tracker remember their positions separately. The route toolbar holds the destination search, **Refresh** and **More**; **More** opens **Multi-route**, **Currency vendors**, **Zone phases** and the two debug copies. Currency results combine the included catalogue with your observed merchants and filter known access requirements. Search accepts NPC/quest names or IDs. Reference quest coordinates are labeled separately from live quest objectives and turn-ins.

In the Teleports tab, **left-click a missing item** to open its source details in ALL THE THINGS (ATT). If ATT is unavailable, QuickRoute opens its own help. **Right-click**, or use **How to obtain** in list view, to open QuickRoute's help directly. It combines available requirements with a short ATT source preview, a copyable Wowhead link and a route button for known source positions. Unknown positions remain explicit. Account-wide toy ownership does not make that toy usable by every race, class or profession.

Trips support up to 20 stops and persist per character. Up to ten stops use an exact shortest-order solver for the estimated reusable-route matrix; larger lists use a bounded optimization heuristic. The matrix keeps a teleport whose catalogue record states a cooldown of zero, because that one is available for every leg; a teleport with a cooldown, or with none recorded, stays out of it. The matrix uses the phase/access state available during comparison. Each executable leg is recalculated from your actual position and available teleports. Confirm a reached stop to continue. Random landings are not presented as exact teleport destinations.

A missing route means the addon lacks a usable recorded connection or required state; it does not prove the destination is inaccessible in the game. Known hearth inns are resolved automatically from their localized name. Morgenluft uses the current Midnight inn as its default; an observed arrival or binding overrides it, including a binding in the legacy area. Other unknown or ambiguous inns require an observed arrival or binding. Catalogue coordinates approximate the inn, not the precise landing; [coverage and sources](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/blob/main/docs/data/hearthstone-locations.md) describe the limits. Housing destinations require owned-house identity and an observed neighborhood plot position. Phase assumptions never change your character’s actual phase or mark an unperformed Zidormi conversation complete.

## For addon authors

`QuickRouteAPI` is a global table another addon can use to ask QuickRoute for a
route. It is versioned: `QuickRouteAPI:GetVersion()` returns the contract version
this build implements.

```lua
local handle = QuickRouteAPI:CalculateRoute(
    { mapID = 84, x = 0.5, y = 0.6, title = "Stormwind", role = "objective", owner = "MyAddon" },
    function(route, failure)
        if not route then
            print("no route:", failure.reason, failure.retryable)
            return
        end
        print(route.totalTime, #route.steps)
    end
)
-- Later, if the answer is no longer wanted:
QuickRouteAPI:Cancel(handle)
```

What the contract guarantees:

- For every request that returns a handle, the callback receives either a
  route or a named failure, never silence. A request superseded by a newer one
  is told so. A malformed request returns no handle and the failure
  `invalid_request`, and its callback is not called.
- `owner` is optional: a non-empty string, usually your addon's name. A new
  request with an owner replaces that owner's earlier request, which is told
  `superseded`. It never replaces another owner's request. Requests without an
  owner run independently and end only with their answer or with `Cancel`.
  Contract version 2 introduced this; in version 1 any addon's request
  replaced any other's.
- One route is calculated at a time, and every waiting request delays the
  player's own. At most `QuickRouteAPI.MAX_PENDING` (8) requests wait at once.
  Past that, the request still returns a handle, and its callback receives the
  retryable failure `busy` on the next frame. A request from an owner that
  already has one waiting is
  always taken, because it replaces that one. An addon that asks often should
  pass an `owner` or `Cancel` the requests it no longer needs.
- The result is a detached copy. Only the fields the contract names cross the
  boundary, so an internal rename cannot break a consumer.
- `route.assumptions` states what the estimate rests on: which maps have unknown
  movement eligibility, whether a flight time is a distance heuristic, and which
  legs land on a guessed position rather than an observed one.
- Nothing in the contract sets a waypoint, moves your arrow or starts travel.

`QuickRouteAPI:RejectStep(from, to, destination)` and `AcceptStep(from, to)` are
the same refusal the "Cannot use" button makes, for a consumer that renders its
own step list. A refusal applies to the destination it was made for and is never
written to disk.

## Dependencies

**Optional:**
- [TomTom](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/tomtom) (for waypoint integration)
- [ALL THE THINGS](https://github.com/ATTWoWAddon/AllTheThings) (for missing-item source details; QuickRoute also works without it)

## Supported Teleports

### Items & Toys
- Hearthstones (regular, Dalaran, Garrison)
- Kirin Tor Rings (all variants)
- Tabards (Argent Crusader's, Tol Barad)
- Engineering devices (Wormhole Generators, Dimensional Rippers)
- Various toys (Direbrew's Remote, Tome of Town Portal, etc.)

### Class Spells
- **Mage:** Recorded city teleports, including Shattrath, Dalaran, Valdrakken and Dornogal
- **Druid:** Teleport: Moonglade, Dreamwalk
- **Monk:** Zen Pilgrimage
- **Death Knight:** Death Gate
- **Shaman:** Astral Recall
- **Demon Hunter:** Fel Retreat

### Portals
- Major hubs: Stormwind, Orgrimmar, Dalaran, Oribos, Valdrakken, Dornogal
- Boats, zeppelins, trams
- Druid Dreamway network

## Development

### Linting
```bash
# Install luacheck (requires LuaRocks)
luarocks install luacheck

# Run linter
./scripts/lint.sh
# or
luacheck QuickRoute/ --config .luacheckrc
```

### Important: WoW uses Lua 5.1
- No `goto` statements (added in Lua 5.2)
- No bitwise operators like `&`, `|` (use `bit.band`, `bit.bor`)
- No `//` floor division (use `math.floor`)

### CI
GitHub Actions automatically runs luacheck and syntax validation on PRs.

## License

MIT License - See LICENSE file for details.

Adapted destination and transport data retain their upstream notices: [Mapzeroth](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/blob/main/QuickRoute/ThirdParty/Mapzeroth-NOTICE.md) and [AllTheThings](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/blob/main/QuickRoute/Licenses/AllTheThings-MIT.txt). The [catalogue source manifest](https://github.com/CybotTM/wow-quickroute/blob/main/QuickRoute/Data/DestinationCatalog.sources.txt) pins the input revision and file hashes. Regenerate with `python3 scripts/generate_destination_catalog.py --help`; upstream Lua is parsed as data and never executed.

## QuickRoute v1.22.0

QuickRoute now loads on WoW Forever as well as on retail, from the same download (#122). This release also adds an optional diagnostic trace, a reminder to save recorded data, and turns the zone survey off unless a player switches it on.

### WoW Forever

The addon ships a second TOC, `QuickRoute_Camelot.toc` (interface 16001), which the Forever client loads instead of the retail one. On Forever, routes are built from a Forever data set only, never from retail data:

- Flight points, flight paths, ships and zeppelins come from the Forever client's own tables (build 1.60.1.70862), including the new ship to Rog'mar in the Riverglades and the zeppelins to Zephras Isle.
- Zone neighbours, inns, dungeon entrances and service points are converted from the retail positions into Forever's maps. Where Cataclysm changed the terrain, such as Darkshore or Thousand Needles, these positions are estimates.
- The neighbours of Alterac Mountains, the Riverglades and Shen'dralas are estimated from the map outlines until crossings are observed in game.
- Portal rooms are left out: no Forever table shows them, and a converted retail portal produced routes through portals that do not exist there.

Every Forever zone is reachable from its faction's capital and back.

### Diagnostic trace

A new setting, "Diagnostic trace", keeps a detailed log in SavedVariables: which code opened the route window, waypoint and quest-tracking changes, quest and NPC dialogs, zone changes, loading screens, flights and route calculations. It is off by default, holds at most about 17,000 entries (6 MiB), and drops the oldest entries when full.

### Save reminder

WoW writes addon data to disk only on `/reload` or logout. While the diagnostic trace or the zone survey has unsaved data, a small window offers a reload every 20 minutes, showing what is recorded and how full the trace is. It never appears in combat, on a flight, in a loading screen or in an instance, and it closes after 30 seconds. Both times and the reminder itself can be changed in the settings.

### Zone survey off by default

The zone survey now has its own settings checkbox and is off unless switched on. Versions 1.16.0 to 1.21.2 switched it on by themselves, so this version turns that automatic setting off once and says so in chat; recorded crossings are kept. A crossing during a taxi flight is now recorded separately from one on foot.

### Flight masters in zones without another route node

A flight master in a zone with no other route node, such as Redridge Mountains or Loch Modan, was not used for routes. It is now. Across 6,156 benchmark routes, 58 got faster and none slower.

### Verify your download

The zip attached here carries a build attestation. To check that this workflow, at this commit, produced the exact bytes you downloaded:

```
gh attestation verify QuickRoute-1.22.0.zip --repo CybotTM/wow-quickroute
```

CurseForge and Wago carry no attestation of their own, so this covers the GitHub download only.

### Installation
1. Download `QuickRoute-1.22.0.zip`
2. Extract to `World of Warcraft/_retail_/Interface/AddOns/` (WoW Forever: `World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/`)
3. Restart WoW or `/reload`

## QuickRoute v1.21.2

This release fixes two things that @CybotTM's zone survey showed on a live 12.1.5 client: routes from a sub-zone QuickRoute does not know, and how the survey itself records a loading screen.

### Routes start on foot from unknown sub-zones

Standing in a sub-zone QuickRoute does not know, such as Der Düsterweg in Silvermoon City, a cave or a phased copy of a zone, a route had no way out on foot (#119). From Der Düsterweg to the Silvermoon portal room, the route was a hearthstone to Dalaran and two portals; without a teleport there was no route at all. QuickRoute now places such a position on the parent zone, at the same spot in the world, and the route starts with a walk.

The survey had seen the player walk into 29 such sub-zones with no route out without a teleport. 25 of them now have one. Knardor Isle and the Ring of Glory still have none, because the Coiled Isle around them has no overland link; nor do Acherus and one variant of the Priory.

### The zone survey records the zone, not the continent

Right after a loading screen the client can report the continent for a moment before the zone. The survey then counted the arrival on the continent and the step into the zone as a walk (#118): 41 of 90 loading-screen arrivals ended on a continent map. The survey now waits for the zone and records the crossing there, with the real origin. A stay on a continent longer than 10 seconds records no crossing at all.

If you keep a zone survey, start a new one after updating with `/qrsurvey clear`. The old records hold walks that were loading screens.

### Verify your download

The zip attached here carries a build attestation. To check that this workflow, at this commit, produced the exact bytes you downloaded:

```
gh attestation verify QuickRoute-1.21.2.zip --repo CybotTM/wow-quickroute
```

CurseForge and Wago carry no attestation of their own, so this covers the GitHub download only.

### Installation
1. Download `QuickRoute-1.21.2.zip`
2. Extract to `World of Warcraft/_retail_/Interface/AddOns/`
3. Restart WoW or `/reload`

## QuickRoute v1.21.1

This release declares WoW 12.1.5, so the client no longer lists QuickRoute as out of date, and applies what the addon's zone survey recorded on a live 12.1.5 client.

### Ready for WoW 12.1.5

The addon now declares interface 120105 (#109). Live retail moved to 12.1.5 on 2026-10-16. None of the game functions or events removed between 12.1.0 and 12.1.5 is used by QuickRoute.

### The Arcantina key lands in the Arcantina

@CybotTM read the zone survey and found three arrivals, from Azj-Kahet, Silithus and Moonglade, that all landed on the same point in the Arcantina (#110). QuickRoute had the Personal Key to the Arcantina landing in Silvermoon City instead, so a route by the key started in the city and left out the way out. The key now lands in the Arcantina, and the route continues through the Arcantina exit to Silvermoon City.

### Four more places to walk from

The survey also recorded walks without a loading screen into four places QuickRoute did not know. They are now connected on foot to the zones around them:

- Northshire and Elwynn Forest
- Atal'Aman, with Zul'Aman and Eversong Woods
- City of Threads - Lower and Azj-Kahet
- The Grudge Pit and Harandar

The travel times are estimates, like the other overland times in QuickRoute.

## QuickRoute v1.21.0

This release fixes what an external review of 1.20.0 found in how routes arrive over several frames: a closed window that opened again, a dungeon quest that sent you back out, and a pasted waypoint read the wrong way without a word. For addon authors, `QuickRouteAPI` moves to contract version 2.

### A closed window stays closed

A route that is calculated over several frames used to open the QuickRoute window when it arrived, even if you had closed it in the meantime. @CybotTM traced that through every place a route arrives late: a map click, `/qrwp`, the next stop of a trip and the currency vendor search. The window now stays closed; the destination is kept, and the window routes there the next time you open it. A window that was already closed when you asked for the route still opens, and a window you closed and opened again shows the new route.

### Inside a dungeon quest's instance, you stay there

QuickRoute checked whether you were already inside a quest's dungeon with the wrong kind of map id, so the answer was often "no" and you were routed back to the entrance. It now asks the client with the instance's own map id.

### A waypoint with two readings asks which one you mean

`/way #2393 50,57 56 Treasure` is either 50.57, 56 with the label "Treasure" or 50, 57 with the label "56 Treasure". The trip window used to pick the second without telling you. It now shows both readings with a button for each and imports nothing until you choose. A coordinate is also read as one whole token, so a decimal comma is no longer split into a number and a label, and a pair that mixes a decimal point with a decimal comma is refused as ambiguous.

### Map clicks no longer freeze a frame

The route panel, a map click and `/qrwp` now calculate in budgeted slices across frames, like the dungeon group offer already did. The window opens when the route is ready. Requests from different places queue instead of cancelling each other.

### For addon authors: `QuickRouteAPI` contract version 2

`QuickRouteAPI:GetVersion()` returns 2. One addon's request no longer replaces another addon's:

- A request can name an `owner`. A new request replaces only the same owner's earlier one, including an answer that was calculated but not yet delivered, which is told `superseded`.
- Without an `owner`, requests run independently and end only with their answer or with `Cancel`. An addon that relied on its second request replacing its first passes the same `owner` on both, or cancels the first.
- At most eight requests wait at once. Past that, the request still gets a handle and its callback receives the retryable failure `busy` on the next frame.
- The undocumented `QuickRouteAPI:NotifySuperseded()` is removed.

The README section "For addon authors" has the details.

### Smaller changes

A dungeon route whose group offer has already ended is no longer shown, and the offered dungeon is resolved from its group finder activity correctly. The retail acceptance checklist now requires a real dungeon offer as the positive case and measures whole-frame times.

## QuickRoute v1.20.0

QuickRoute answers one question: how does this character get to that place? This release makes it say more about the answer — why a route could not be produced, which landing points are guesses, and what a destination actually is — and adds a contract other addons can call.

### Your hearthstone is on the map before you use it

An existing hearthstone binding used to be invisible to routing until QuickRoute watched you use it. @CybotTM sourced and audited the catalogue behind this. The bound inn is now resolved from the client's localized bind name against a sourced catalogue of 59 destinations on 44 maps, audited against the retail 12.1.0 area table in all eleven supported locales. An observed binding always wins over the catalogue, and a catalogue position is labelled as approximate in the tooltip rather than presented as exact.

### A failed route says what went wrong

`CalculatePath` returned nothing whether your position was not available yet, the route needed something this character does not have, the only known way was one you refused, or nothing connects the two points at all. Those need different responses from you, so they are no longer one blank answer.

### "Cannot use" on a step

A step you cannot take gets a button. QuickRoute keeps the destination, drops that one connection for this route and looks for another way. Right-clicking Refresh takes your refusals back. Nothing is written to disk and nothing is treated as unlock data.

### One search can no longer own a frame

A long calculation now continues across frames on a measured budget instead of holding the client until it finishes.

### The trip you chose is not thrown away

A destination you pick can be locked. An interruption — an accepted dungeon invitation, an alert — suspends it and gives it back afterwards, still locked. Accepting a group invitation offers the route to that dungeon's entrance rather than silently replacing where you were going.

### Other addons can ask for a route

`QuickRouteAPI` is a versioned contract: ask for a route, get a detached result or a named failure, cancel what you asked for. It states what the estimate assumes, including which legs land on a catalogue guess rather than an observed position, and it never sets a waypoint or starts travel. The README has a worked example.

### Smaller changes

Destination search is ordered by what you typed — exact name, then prefix, then word start, then substring. Silvermoon is offered to both factions; it was marked Horde, so Alliance characters never saw it. A leg on a map you are not standing on is priced from what that zone allows. The trip window accepts the waypoint forms players actually paste, including several `/way` lines on one line and decimal commas. A destination now carries a role — objective, hand-in, reference, service, entrance — so a quest that is not in your log is not presented as an active objective.

The zip attached here carries a build attestation. To check that this workflow, at this commit, produced the exact bytes you downloaded:
